Subject and Object Relative Clauses
You can use subject and object relative clauses to provide additional information without repeating the subject.

When you use a subject or an object relative clause, you are introducing new information with a subordinate clause instead of repeating the subject again.

  • This is the new software. This software has new features. (Repeated subject.)

Instead you can say:

  • This is the new software, which has new features.

Depending on the subject or object you are talking about, you need to select the appropriate relative pronoun. Look at the chart below to learn more about the relative pronouns.

The client computer, which is also known as a workstation, is the computer a person uses to access files and applications through a network.
The server is a computer which serves and supports multiple users to log in and provides service and access to different files.
The Client and the Server Computers
There are different roles for computers in a network, and most of them are clients, and there is usually one server.

The client and the server are parts of a model of computing distribution.

Usually, there is one server in a network that sends responses to clients’ requests, therefore, the server is always waiting for it. Sometimes it might be necessary for the server to contact other servers to reply the requested data; it can request passwords from clients and host multiple clients.

On the other hand, the client computer is also known as the initiator since it is used by the end user. This is the one that requests information to the server.  

A client is a small machine with basic hardware, which allows the user to browse and do simple commands, in contrast to the server, which has higher configurations and is a more powerful machine.
The server is a computer which serves and supports multiple users to log in, provides service and access to different files.
A client can perform simple tasks, and requests information to the server.

images.text:
Kim: Joe, help me catch up. What was the main topic you studied during the class yesterday?
Joe: Mr. Smith explained the difference between a client and a server computer.
Kim: I see, and what is the main difference?
Joe: Well, the client computer, which is also known as a workstation, is the computer a person uses to access files and applications through a network. This machine is less expensive and more basic in terms of software. A client can perform simple tasks and request information to the server.
Kim: So, a client computer is the one we usually use. What about the server?

Joe: The server is a computer which serves and supports multiple users to log in and provides service and access to different files. This is called the client-server model, and its use has increased over the past few years.
Kim: What about the software they use?
Joe: Server computers use an operating system that is specifically designed for that use. There are different operating systems (OS) created by the main computer companies. Most of the time you need to pay for a license to use them, and there are just a few which are free; among their main features are cross-platform, file sharing, authentication services, networking, and web hosting.

Kim: And the OS for the client computers?
Joe: There have been traditionally two main OSs which are used by clients all around the world. Both need a license. Although they might share some similarities, there are certain substantial differences between them, including compatibility, manufacturing, distribution, cost and design. However, there are plenty more available, including free license software and other alternative operating systems.
